references.text: God speaks to Abram in a vision and says 'Do not be afraid', paralleling God's address to Abraham in Genesis 22:1.
God tested Israel in the wilderness to know their heart, just as He tested Abraham in Genesis 22:1.
The Lord tests His people to see if they love Him with all their hearts – the same theme as God's testing of Abraham.
Samuel answers 'Here I am' (Hineni) when the Lord calls him, parallel to Abraham's response in Genesis 22:1.
Isaiah answers 'Here I am, send me' – a parallel to Abraham's willing response 'Hineni' when God calls.
Hebrews 11:17-19 comments directly on Abraham's faith when he was tested and was willing to offer Isaac.
James 2:21-23 discusses Abraham's justification by works, especially his willingness to offer Isaac as described in Genesis 22.
A direct narrative connection showing Abraham's continued obedience during the test.
The New Testament's theological interpretation of Abraham's faith in the test.
Highlights the consequence of Abraham's obedience for his descendants.
The link between faith and works: the test in 22:1 completes the faith.
The conclusion of the same event showing God's provision.
Clarifies the purpose of Abraham's selection and obedience.
Confirms that Abraham's obedience (including the test) was the basis for the blessing.
A direct part of the same event showing Abraham's faith in God's provision.
